key_insight: User simulators in agent benchmarks can materially change outcomes, so they should be evaluated for fidelity—not just the agent.
engineering_relevance: For benchmark design and multi-turn RL training, selecting a low-cost but faithful user proxy is critical because simulator behavior can alter tool use and reward while still passing unseen user-role checks.
method: Built UserProxyBench as an evaluation layer on the tau-bench family.
Introduced User Fidelity Score (UFS) to score adherence to private user instructions with task-grounded rubrics.
Compared seven user proxies across enterprise tasks to map a cost-fidelity frontier.
evidence_signal: With GPT-5.5 held fixed, changing only the user proxy across 375 enterprise tasks shifted mean task reward by 15.2 points, and 24.4% of successful episodes still contained a user-specification violation.
watch_item: A proxy can preserve task reward while subtly changing the interaction pattern, so benchmark results may be misleading unless simulator fidelity is checked directly.
paper_title: UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training
